blocks.orig: 8 DAYS CHIMPANZEE SAFARI GOMBE STREAM + MAHALE MOUNTAINS
blocks.html: 8-day chimpanzee safari to Gombe Stream and the Mahale Mountains

blocks.orig: This is a perfect safari combination to see chimpanzee up close in western Tanzania. Gombe Stream National Park is the famous place where Jane Goodall did her research on chimpanzee populations. It is located on the western border of Tanzania and the Congo, and it has 35 km² of protected land along the hills of the eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika. Mahale Mountains National Park is located close by, south of the city of Kigoma. It is the only place where chimpanzees and lions co-exist.
blocks.html: If you want to see chimpanzees at close range in western Tanzania, this safari combination is ideal. Gombe Stream National Park is the well-known spot where Jane Goodall carried out her research into chimpanzee populations. It sits on Tanzania’s western border with the Congo and protects 35 km² of land on the hills along the eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika. Not far away, south of the town of Kigoma, you’ll find Mahale Mountains National Park, the only place where chimpanzees and lions live side by side.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.

blocks.orig: Have you always dreamed of seeing chimps in their natural habitat? Then by all means visit the Gombe Stream National Park where Jane Goodall once did her behavioural research on chimpanzee populations. This small national park lies along the western border of Tanzania on the eastern shores of Lake Tanganyika, where it is only accessible by boat. Step into the footsteps of Jane Goodall as a guide takes you to watch groups of chimpanzees climb trees, play or nurse their babies!
blocks.html: Have you always wanted to see chimps in the wild? Then make sure you visit Gombe Stream National Park, where Jane Goodall once studied the behaviour of chimpanzee populations. This small park lies on Tanzania’s western border, on the eastern shores of Lake Tanganyika, and can only be reached by boat. Follow in Jane Goodall’s footsteps as a guide leads you to watch groups of chimpanzees climbing trees, playing or nursing their young!

blocks.orig: More chimpanzees await you in the Mahale Mountains National Park. At a 2.5-hour drive and a boat ride from Gombe National Park, this park is a bit larger and home to roughly 900 wild chimpanzees. The park is different from most since there are no roads and you have to go on foot. Experienced guides take you on a hike through the mountains in search of groups of chimpanzees. Once found, you get plenty of time to observe these beauties - a magical experience!
